A densely cluttered outdoor workshop or repair shack sits beneath a canopy of leafy trees, its weathered concrete walls nearly hidden behind decades of salvaged machinery, tangled wires, cages, fans, lamps, and rusted metal. At the top center, a huge circular assemblage resembling a mechanical sunburst dominates the wall. Rust-red and orange metal strips, gears, numbers, plates, and miscellaneous machine parts radiate outward from a round central hub. Thick tree limbs arch across the roof while vines and long aerial roots hang down around the structure. Below the sunburst, old industrial fans, wire cages, lanterns, gauges, pipes, and electrical components crowd nearly every available surface. A narrow, heavily corroded machine cabinet stands upright in the center, fitted with dials, gauges, and a circular clock-like instrument. A large metal fan is mounted to its right, with a battered spherical machine housing beneath it. Across the foreground, a rusty black bicycle leans against the workshop, its frame and wheels partially obscuring more discarded equipment. Potted flowers and green plants soften the lower edges of the scene.
